binders: A dimension m, vector field q, real matrix A, point x,t, and vector qx.
hypotheses: The spatial slice xi -> q(xi,t) has derivative qx at x.
conclusions: The conservative residual q_t + d/dx(A q)=0 at (x,t) holds if and only if the linear-system residual q_t+A q_x=0 holds there.
mathematical_definitions: Each residual predicate existentially witnesses the relevant time and space derivative values.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For a constant real matrix A, once the spatial derivative q_x is known at a point, writing the equation in conservative form with flux F(q)=Aq is equivalent at that point to writing q_t+Aq_x=0.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The equivalence is pointwise and assumes only the spatial derivative; if the time derivative does not exist, both residual predicates may be false.
The dimension m may be zero.
The matrix is constant, and the theorem states no global solution, regularity, initial data, or uniqueness result.
